song.title: A Perfect Day In Spring
song.author: Mark and Helen Johnson
song.summary: Light and breezy, feel-good and carefree, this song seeks to capture the spirit of the season. The chorus encourages us to engage all our senses to fully appreciate the joy of spring. The simple two-part singing helps bring it all together. ‘Could there be a better time of year?’
song.teachingTips:
• Ask the children about the character of the song. What clues are in the music? It has a lively tempo and a cheerful tune. They might also mention the lyrics – words such as ‘perfect’, ‘beautiful’, ‘happy’, ‘haven’t got a care’. 
  • There is quite a lot of melodic repetition in this song which makes it easy to learn. The Words on Screen program is a brilliant aid to teaching the song line by line. 
  • The melody of this song contains some leaps. Practise the top B to low C in bar 5 ‘of year’ and bar 9 ‘be here’ to make sure this interval is clear and that there is no swooping down to the lower note. 
  • This is good song to use to try out part-singing for the first time, as the harmony part (the bridge) has already been introduced earlier in the song.

assembly.title: Super Seeds
assembly.description: This assembly encourages us to look at the potential of seeds for new life and growth and also provides an opportunity to explore our own potential.

assembly.title: Light and Colour
assembly.description: This assembly encourages us to open our eyes to the colours of springtime, talking about our favourite colours, noticing the extra daylight and appreciating nature's use of colour and light.

assembly.title: Extra Energy
assembly.description: What wakes you up in the morning? From birdsong to sprouting leaves and Easter eggs, this assembly helps us to celebrate all the energy of springtime.

assembly.title: People Who Care
assembly.description: The ideal assembly to help us to focus on, appreciate and celebrate all those who help and care for us.

assembly.title: The World Around
assembly.description: From the tallest trees, to the something you can only see with a microscope, this assembly encourages us to notice, appreciate and be thankful for the world around us.

assembly.title: Happy Endings
assembly.description: This assembly explores setbacks we might encounter in our lives and the characteristics needed to overcome them.

assembly.title: Feeling Hopeful
assembly.description: This assembly explores the meaning of hope and what it will take to realize our ambitions for the future.

assembly.title: Feeling Awake
assembly.description: This assembly uses The Parable of the Sower to reflect on what is needed to be ‘awake and ready for action’ in school.

assembly.title: Feeling Good
assembly.description: This assembly explores the uniqueness of human beings and how we can help others to feel more valuable.

resources.title: Flower Graphic Score
resources.content:
[{"key":"7bad39b7a641ea0a","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To play musical instruments while following a graphic score
  • To explore dynamics
  • To recognize repeated melodic patterns
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"ccda70bcff154252","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Untuned percussion, sheets of paper and pens/paints

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"451bbd171e4db451","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Discuss the words of the song. What happens in spring? Why does the song talk about colours blooming everywhere? 

In groups of about three, use A3 sheets of paper and five coloured pens or paints to create flower pictures – have some pictures with just one flower and others with two or three, but make sure each individual flower is painted with only one colour.

With the children, choose an untuned percussion instrument to represent each colour, e.g. yellow/tambourine; orange/guiro; purple/triangle etc. Arrange the pictures on a ‘washing line’ or wall/window to make a score. Follow the score using a pointer, either with the whole class or a group. The children should play their instruments (in any rhythm or style) as their coloured flower appears.

What happens when just one flower is shown? What happens when more than one flower appears on a picture? (It will change the musical texture.)

","title":"Make a graphic score! ","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"cca5934f6a1951b4","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

What other musical dimensions can you add to your graphic score? Perhaps use differently sized flowers to indicate dynamics – playing more quietly ( p) or loudly ( f).

","title":"Step It Up!","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1873-1614695091mFFrP.png"}},{"key":"25525cbf16afbfc0","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Throughout this song, the melody line of ‘Could there be a better time of year?’ is repeated twelve times, with different words. Can the children draw a rainbow in the air with their arms every time this tune is heard?

","title":"Branch Out","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1874-1614695090s5QJx.png"}}]
resources.summary: Create a graphic score and use this to explore musical sounds, textures, tempo and dynamics. Play your composition together as an ensemble following your graphic score.

resources.title: Playing Classical Music (Spring)
resources.content:
[{"key":"8de421d31e95fe11","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Make it a routine to play some classical music at the beginning of the day – perhaps when the children are taking off their coats, settling in the classroom or entering an assembly. Here are a few ideas: 

  • Ballet of the Unhatched Chicks (Mussorgsky)
  • The Lark Ascending (Vaughan-Williams)
  • On Hearing the First Cuckoo in Spring (Delius) 
  • Spring from The Four Seasons (Vivaldi) 
","title":"Music","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: The Arrival Of Spring
resources.content:
[{"key":"e6936f3f06a10794","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

David Hockney (b. 1937) recently made a series of works responding to the changing colours of woodland (Wold Woods, Yorkshire) throughout the four seasons. He created oil paintings, charcoal drawings and iPad drawings, and recorded films as part of this series of work. 

How could the children use the influence of Hockney's work to respond to the colours and changing nature of spring? 

  • Take photos of the school grounds (field/flower beds/nature area) thoughout the seasons to see how things have grown and changed. (Record in a school/class calendar to carry on throughout the year.)
  • Record films of the school grounds. 
  • Incorporate technology to embrace Hockney's style: use iPads or tablets to create spring drawings and play back the creation of these to watch how they form the finished work. 
","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: Planting Project
resources.content:
[{"key":"b1349c66455145d6","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Abraham Cruzvillegas (b. 1968) is a conceptual artist who creates sculptures and installations using found, recycled objects. 

In homage to Cruzvillegas' Empty Lot exhibition at Tate Modern, organize a planting project; ask the children to bring a small plant from their garden or a seed or a bulb from home. Find an area in the school garden, or use a colletion of indoor pot plants for the classroom. Plant the bulbs and seeds and study their growth throughout the season. Think about whether this could be photographed or recorded some way through drawing. How could you make it into a sculptural project? 

","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: Acrostic Spring Poem
resources.content:
[{"key":"482384050edd82de","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Compose an Acrostic Spring Poem. As a class, brainstorm and collect ideas for each of the letters of SPRING. Then, ask the children to write some SPRING poems developing their favourite ideas/words into a line for each letter. 

  • Sunshine peeping through the grey,
  • Petals sprouting, on their way.
  • Rainbows arching overhead, 
  • Insects waking from their beds,
  • New life blooming everywhere,
  • Growing wild, without a care!
","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.content:
[{"key":"c10ba386940b987c","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Ideal for 2-3 sessions

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"2a5c3f90fd6ba697","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To explore musical texture
  • To play musical instruments while following a graphic score
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"3af97533c175435e","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

A selection of untuned percussion instruments; A3 paper; coloured pens or paints 

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"be7c6e9cfebe0f19","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Dynamics; quietly (); loudly ( ); texture; conductor; graphic score

","title":"Key vocabulary","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/icons-keyvocab-280x280-27-1620218359Ng3ET.png"}},{"key":"f30f3e398ae65f45","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Make a graphic score! Discuss the themes of the springtime songs. What happens in spring? In A Perfect Day In Spring, the song talks about colours blooming everywhere. Explore the lyrics of the songs to find other references to plants and flowers growing.

In groups of about three, use A3 sheets of paper and five coloured pens or paints to create flower pictures – have some pictures with just one flower and others with two or three, but make sure each individual flower is painted with only one colour.

With the children, choose an untuned percussion instrument to represent each colour, e.g. yellow/tambourine; orange/guiro; purple/triangle etc. Arrange the pictures on a ‘washing line’ or wall/window to make a score.

Follow the score using a pointer, either with the whole class or a group. The children should play their instruments (in any rhythm or style) as their coloured flower appears. What happens when just one flower is shown? What happens when more than one flower appears on a picture? (It will change the musical texture.)

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"3d236b6b6921889e","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

What other musical dimensions could be added to the graphic score? Perhaps use differently sized flowers to indicate dynamics – playing more quietly () or loudly ( ).

","title":"Step It Up!","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1873-1614695091mFFrP.png"}},{"key":"23c0983128913639","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Many composers have been inspired to write music influenced by springtime, and some have dedicated a whole symphony to the theme, for example Schumann. Have a listen to extracts from Schumann’s Spring Symphony (Symphony No. 1) or listen out for the cuckoo in On Hearing The First Cuckoo In Spring by Delius. Why not try using both pieces to inspire some spring-themed paintings?

","title":"Listen","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/listen-01-1615991956LRT6z.png"}},{"key":"a8d85683f723cb1b","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4x-82HBqTkA","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"9edceb76a446bff7","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FyPSbLWNX0c","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"55ef409ac790cf83","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"Assessment Suggestions","background_color":"#009CCF"}},{"key":"cc2a67692bc6aef8","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"
  • Can they choose, order and combine sounds within a simple structure?
  • Can they follow a simple graphic score (pictorial)?
  • Can they join in and stop at the correct time when playing?
","title":"","noMargin":false}}]

resources.title: Composition Wheels
resources.content:
[{"key":"bc73fc2fd761bc87","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Ideal for 2 sessions

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"8cb4e0c157348b35","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To recognize different instrumental timbres and their effects
  • To combine several layers of sound and describe the effect
  • To create and follow a graphic score
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"e59388d2409e6c52","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Large sheets of paper; pens; card; split pins; tuned and untuned percussion instruments

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"174544d6ec695e53","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Dynamics; forte; loud/strong; piano; soft; tempo; fast; slow; timbre; texture; musical layers; conductor; graphic score 

","title":"Key vocabulary","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/icons-keyvocab-280x280-27-1620218359Ng3ET.png"}},{"key":"44f524b885f25e5e","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

The songs chosen for this activity are based on the theme of ‘morning’.  

Arrange the class into groups and provide a large sheet of paper and pens for each group.  

Listen to Sun Arise and ask the class to draw images inspired by the song. As well as visual ideas such as sun, trees etc., encourage the class to think about different sounds, colours and moods that come to mind as they listen.  

Next, provide a selection of instruments for each group and ask them to think about different ways to represent the ideas on their paper using their instruments, and vocal and body sounds (e.g. whistling for birds singing, shakers for rustling trees, a cymbal played with a soft beater to represent warmth, chimes for the blowing breeze).

Encourage the group to think about varying musical dimensions such as dynamics or tempo to achieve the different effects.

Once the children have collected a range of different sounds, assign a different abstract symbol to each, e.g.  

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"97d5762d2fef9738","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicCurriculum/MusicCurr-ASSETS/year3/year3-musiccurr-compositionwheels-1635426932mDdX7.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"387ffb5cf078855a","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Composition Wheels 

Next, draw three concentric circles on a piece of card and plot the symbols in different parts of the circle. Then, create a pointer and attach it to the centre of the card using a split pin. Create one wheel for each group. One member of the group takes the role of ‘conductor’ and spins the pointer, while the other members of the group play the corresponding sounds. Discuss how the texture changes at every spin as more sounds are added or taken away. Explain that this is a form of graphic score.  

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"cf83582859a81d64","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicCurriculum/MusicCurr-ASSETS/year3/year3-musiccurr-compositionwheels2-1635426933CyeXk.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"850dec424281d2b2","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Try using the Composition Wheels as an introduction to a performance of Sun Arise.  

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"a27da1f2af37162a","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Create a whole-class composition by asking each of the groups to perform their composition wheels together. One member of each group should spin the pointer to change the musical texture, and a signal to end the music should be agreed.  

","title":"Step It Up!","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1873-1614695091mFFrP.png"}},{"key":"5433285c2ede912f","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicCurriculum/MusicCurr-ASSETS/year3/year3-musiccurr-compositionwheels3-16354269341DcpD.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"ff9c021619cd6887","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Challenge the children to create their own Composition Wheels based on a chosen theme (e.g. space, the Great Fire of London, rainforests, rivers). 

","title":"Branch Out","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1874-1614695090s5QJx.png"}},{"key":"68960506c7b26305","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

How have other composers interpreted the theme of morning? Listen to ‘Morning Mood’ from Peer Gynt Suite No. 1  by Edvard Grieg, or use one of the song choices and get the children to draw what they hear. 

","title":"Listen","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/listen-01-1615991956LRT6z.png"}},{"key":"c039191895b47b7c","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J-1Bob1dU18","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"e41f4e742da6de03","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"Assessment Suggestions","background_color":"#009CCF"}},{"key":"83996eec1eadc143","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"
  • Can they respond imaginatively to music, describing the ideas and images it evokes? 
  • Can they investigate different ways of using voices, body percussion and instruments to achieve an effect? 
  • Can they create and follow graphic notation? 
  • Can they give performance directions (e.g. taking the role of conductor)?
","title":"","noMargin":false}}]
